https://www.thedailybeast.com/manosphere.text: Politics Barron’s Butch Buddy Issues Stark Warning to Trump HELP OR ELSE The arrest of manosphere influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate has raised concerns about the brothers’ clout in right-wing political circles. Mary Papenfuss Reporter Updated Aug. 2 2026 3:21AM EDT / Published Aug. 2 2026 1:22AM EDT Comments DANIEL MIHAILESCU/AFP via Getty Images “Manosphere” influencer Andrew Tate, who has been linked to Barron Trump and the president, issued a pointed call for Donald Trump to help him and his brother fight the sex trafficking charges they are facing. The attorney for the right-wing, self-described misogynists—Andrew, 38, and Tristan, 39—warned Republicans of a mysterious reckoning if Trump fails to help the embattled brothers in their legal battle against the 59 rape and sex trafficking charges filed against them by British authorities. Tristan (left) and brother Andrew Tate speak to reporters. DANIEL MIHAILESCU/AFP via Getty Images The brothers, who have dual American-British citizenship, have denied any wrongdoing. They’ve been in a Miami jail since July 18, when they were arrested on the new U.K. charges. The United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service is now seeking their extradition to the U.K. “Andrew Tate was a material participant in ensuring President Trump’s victory,” the Tates’ lawyer , Joseph McBride, told Vanity Fair in an article published Thursday. “If Trump doesn’t support him, and if the next people who are going to be running for office potentially are just like, ‘Yeah, down the river he goes,’ that young cohort of people will break with the Republican Party in the next election,” McBride warned. Barron Buddy Andrew Tate Mocked Over Heinous Arrest Outfits FASHION POLICE Cameron Adams He also added in a later Instagram post that New York Democratic Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez “will be the next President without the manosphere and Andrew Tate.” Trump, 80, has not responded to the warning. But White House spokesperson Karoline Leavitt said “no” when asked by reporters if the president would help the Tates. The Tates fled to Fort Lauderdale, Florida, last year from Romania, where they were living, when Romanian prosecutors suddenly lifted travel restrictions that had been keeping them in the country amid criminal investigations. The Trump administration did nothing to block their entry into the U.S. or to hold them on outstanding overseas charges. Some reports have indicated that the administration may have pressured Romanian officials to lift the brothers’ travel restrictions. The Tates, who wield clout in right-wing American political circles, freely spread their anti-feminist views on Elon Musk’s X and other social media platforms. Barron Trump and his sister Ivanka wait for dad to deliver the State of the Union address earlier this year. Evelyn Hockstein/REUTERS PBS and The New York Times have reported that Trump’s 20-year-old son Barron talked with Andrew Tate on the phone during the 2024 presidential election, although the Trump family has denied the reports. “Andrew Tate was very… strategic and shrewd in cultivating these alliances with people on the American right, including in the Trump family,” Times reporter Megan Twohey said in a PBS interview late last year . The Daily Beast has reached out to the White House for comment. Barron Dragged Into Probe of His Twisted Rape Charge Idols TATE EXPECTATIONS Cameron Adams Barron Trump has reportedly been “a fan of Andrew, and they actually spoke by Zoom… with a mutual friend, who told me… that they discussed the Romanian case and how they thought it was just an effort to silence the Tates,” Twohey said. The mutual friend also told her it was a “politically motivated criminal investigation.” Mary Papenfuss Reporter mary.papenfuss@thedailybeast.com Got a tip? Send it to The Daily Beast here . https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/12/dron.text: An oil pipeline in Saudi Arabia, deemed "essential" for bypassing the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, has been shut down after a fire that, according to the authorities, followed a drone attack launched from Iraq.The East-West pipeline links Abqaiq, near the Persian Gulf, to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, and is used as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz for transporting Saudi oil to the Red Sea. A statement from the Saudi foreign ministry referred to a fire near Medina, said to have caused "human and material damage".A government official in Riyadh had already told the media that people had been injured in the drone attack and the subsequent blaze. The same official said the pipeline had been shut down as a precaution.The Iraqi government acknowledged that the attack was launched from its territory and announced that it had dismissed the commander of Maysan province in the south of the country as a consequence.Saudi Arabia frequently accuses Iran-linked armed groups based in neighbouring Iraq of targeting its oil facilities with drones.The Gulf Cooperation Council, which brings together six countries in the region, issued a statement expressing concern and describing the incident as "a dangerous escalation and an unacceptable threat to the security of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia".The government in Riyadh said it would not respond to the attack for the time being, stating that it intended "not to react at this stage and to support the efforts of the Iraqi government to prevent attacks launched from its territory against the Saudi kingdom and neighbouring countries".This incident comes just a day after the Houthi rebels in Yemen, backed by Iran, took control of an island of strategic importance in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a location of crucial importance for global oil trade. It marks an escalation in the Houthis' attempts to block Saudi Arabia's trade; Riyadh backs Yemen's government. According to the rebels, navigation in the strait was "safe for everyone except the Saudis".This latest attack adds another layer to the series of incidents in the war launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February, which has pushed oil and fuel prices to new record highs. The price of a barrel of oil climbed above 100 dollars on Friday, with fuel prices hitting fresh records.

https://www.bursa.ro/textbooks-in-crisis.text: Students entering the 9th grade will start the 2026-2027 school year without printed textbooks corresponding to the new programs. In the most optimistic scenario, digital textbooks could be available at the beginning of the school year, while printed books would arrive in high schools later. The situation brings to mind a problem that has arisen in the education system before: changing school programs and preparing textbooks do not always manage to keep up with the school year calendar. *First generation of high school students with new programs The 2026-2027 school year begins on September 7, and for students entering the 9th grade, the start of high school comes with an important change. They are the first generation to study according to the new high school programs. However, the textbooks related to these programs will not be available in printed format at the beginning of the courses. Bogdan Cristescu, director of the National Center for Curriculum and Evaluation, told Rador in August that the new textbooks will not be physically available on September 7. In the best case, the textbooks will be accessible in digital format at the beginning of the school year, and the printed ones could reach students later, provided that the procedure is not delayed by appeals. Cristescu specified that, if the textbooks are not ready on time, there is also the option of developing methodological guides for teachers. However, the solution is a compromise, at a time when students are just beginning the first stage of a curricular reform. *113 textbooks, a procedure of over 94 million lei The problem did not arise in the last days before the start of school. The acquisition procedure was launched by the Ministry of Education in April. According to the National Center for Curriculum and Evaluation, the procedure concerns 113 textbook titles for grade 9, divided into lots, with a total estimated value of 94,383,293.40 lei. The auction was launched in the Electronic Public Procurement System on April 10, and the deadline for submitting offers was June 9. At the time of launching the procedure, the Ministry of Education provided for contracts with a duration of eight years, which would allow the use of textbooks for a longer period and reduce the need for similar procedures each year. From an administrative point of view, the procedure is complex. The projects submitted by publishing houses must be evaluated, the results must be approved, and in the case of appeals, the procedure may be extended. After completing these stages, teachers must choose the approved variants, schools must centralize the necessary, and the textbooks must be printed and distributed. For students, however, all these steps have a very simple result: on September 7, they will not have the new textbooks on their desks. *The alarm signal came before the auction The fact that the textbooks will not arrive at the beginning of the school year is not a total surprise for those involved in the process. In February, Cristian Greşanu, president of the Romanian Publishers' Union, warned that it was difficult to believe that the new 9th grade textbooks would be able to reach students in September. He explained at the time that, after the auction was launched, periods were needed for evaluation and for possible appeals. The calendar thus had a risk zone from the beginning. The new programs had to be transformed into textbooks, the projects had to be submitted and evaluated, and the winning textbooks had to be contracted, printed, and distributed in a relatively short period of time before the start of classes. In August, the warning turned into certainty: students would not start the year with printed textbooks. *Digital can be a solution, but it does not solve the delay The Ministry and representatives of the education system invoke the possibility of using digital textbooks. It is a solution that can allow teachers to work according to the new programs even if the printed copies are not yet available. For some schools, this can reduce the effects of the delay. However, the digital textbook does not change the fact that printed materials are not available when classes start. In addition, there is also the problem of effective access to technology. The permanent use of an electronic textbook presupposes the existence of appropriate devices and infrastructure, both in school and at home. The Ministry's official platform for digital textbooks already exists and includes textbooks for several grades. For the new grade 9 textbooks, however, the approval and publication process is still ongoing. According to information published at the end of August, for the batches that will not be contested, the digital textbooks could be published by the end of September, with the printed versions to be distributed later. *This is not the first time textbooks have been delayed The current situation is not unique in Romanian education. In September 2023, approximately two weeks after the start of the school year, four textbooks for grades 1, 2 and 6 had not yet arrived in schools. That year, the Ministry stated that 43 new textbooks had been printed and distributed, but four titles were still behind schedule. Problems related to textbooks have also arisen in previous years, especially during periods when the education system was undergoing curricular changes. The current case is different in terms of the scale of the change: the entire 9th grade falls under the new high school programs, and the necessary is covered by a procedure that includes 113 titles. *Curriculum reform begins before textbooks The fundamental problem is synchronization. A curricular reform involves more than just approving school programs. For the change to work in the classroom, textbooks, teaching materials, teacher training and time to adapt to the new requirements are needed. In the case of the 9th grade, the first component is already behind the school calendar. The tender was launched in April, the offers were submitted by June, and the evaluation of the projects ended in August. During this time, the first day of classes remained fixed for September 7. It is the difference between two calendars that should have worked together: the administrative procurement calendar and the school calendar. For the administration, the procedure continues after September 7. For students and teachers, however, school starts then. *The cost of the delay is borne by the schools In the absence of textbooks, teachers have to work with other resources until the books arrive in the high schools. This may mean materials prepared by the teachers, digital resources, or the use of auxiliary materials. In the case of a class that starts high school according to new programs, the problem is more complicated than in the case of a simple delay in the distribution of already existing textbooks. Teachers must build their teaching activity based on the new programs, given that the main tool intended to support them is not yet available in printed form. Cristian Greşanu showed that textbooks are approved in batches and that possible appeals may cause some titles to arrive later than others. Therefore, the moment when all textbooks will actually reach students is not necessarily identical. Articol despre Textbooks, school, students, teachers.

A new online tool, the Carbon Impacts Tracer, allows users to calculate the impact of carbon dioxide emissions from such projects. Photograph: New South Wales Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure View image in fullscreen The Hunter Valley Operations mine in New South Wales, Australia. A new online tool, the Carbon Impacts Tracer, allows users to calculate the impact of carbon dioxide emissions from such projects. Photograph: New South Wales Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure Greenhouse gas emissions Analysis Corporations claim their fossil fuel emissions are a drop in the ocean. But what if we could count the real cost? Graham Readfearn A new tool called Carbon Impacts Tracer can be used to estimate climate impact from emissions across eight metrics, including lost food production Mon 28 Sep 2026 16.00 EDT Last modified on Mon 28 Sep 2026 18.05 EDT Share The biggest coal project before authorities in New South Wales, the HVO mine , will emit the equivalent of about 809m tonnes of climate-warming carbon dioxide if it wins approval. That number, for most people, will carry little meaning, as might the calculation that adding that amount of greenhouse gas to the atmosphere will cause an extra 0.00036C of global heating. But what if the public was instead told that that amount of carbon dioxide would expose almost half a million people to unprecedented heat, or kill nearly 15 million coral colonies on the Great Barrier Reef every time it bleaches? All those statistics come from a new tool that translates the emissions from burning fossil fuels into estimated real-world climate effects taken from peer-reviewed climate studies. Australia’s renewables transition is well under way – but meeting its 2030 target will be ‘extremely challenging’ Read more “Small numbers in global warming can mean catastrophic impacts,” says Prof Sarah Perkins-Kirkpatrick, a climate scientist at the Australian National University who is part of a team launching the Carbon Impacts Tracer . The NSW Independent Planning Commission is expected to make a decision this week about the future of the HVO mine , with the joint owners Yancoal and Glencore hoping to keep digging at the Hunter Valley site until 2045. Plugging the project’s expected emissions into the tracer suggests, for example, the extra heat trapped in the atmosphere by its emissions will reduce crop production every year by an amount that is the equivalent to the minimum dietary requirements of 276,129 people. The tool can be used to estimate the impact of carbon dioxide emissions from any project, company or state – or for any known amount of emissions – across eight different factors including the loss of labour hours due to excess heat, the loss of glaciers, the death of corals or lost food production. Central to the tool is a metric known as Transient Climate Response to CO₂ Emissions (TCRE) – an established calculation that every billion tonnes of CO 2 causes about 0.45C of global heating. Once an amount of CO 2 is known – such as from a major fossil project – it’ contribution to global heating can be calculated and, from there, says Perkins-Kirkpatrick, measured against already published studies. “Every tonne of CO 2 matters and we’ve known this for decades,” she said. “To pinpoint what this means with a high degree of confidence has taken us a long time. This [tool] is to hold big fossil fuel emitters accountable. It is not meant to be a blame game. It just shows that all emissions have impacts and now we can prove it.” All the results are presented as the best estimate within a likely range of uncertainty, with links back to the original scientific studies used for the calculations. 3:01 What is an El Niño and how could it cause the hottest year on record? – video Perkins-Kirkpatrick accepts some may be sceptical of the results, but counters “we are not making these numbers up for shits and giggles”. “This is based on the best analysis published in the peer-reviewed literature,” she said. And this is only the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the impacts [of fossil fuel burning].” The Carbon Impacts Tracer was developed by scientists at the Australian National University, the Australian Research Council Centre of Excellence for the Weather of the 21st Century and the Lethal Humidity Global Council, and was funded by the Minderoo Foundation. Maria Nawaz leads the Australian Climate Accountability Project at the Australian Human Rights Institute at the University of New South Wales – a partner in the tracer project. “One of the major challenges in climate litigation has been establishing a direct link between a government or a corporation’s actions and climate harms and suffering,” she said. “Governments and corporations have argued their emissions are ‘just a drop in the ocean’ and too small to measure. “But we can now refute this defence and show the emissions of any state or corporation can be tied to a global warming figure and then human and ecological harms. It is transformative.” Elaine Johnson, an experienced climate lawyer and director of Johnson Legal but not involved in the work, said there will be governments and corporations that will not welcome the development of the tool. “Fossil fuel companies do not want people to be able to make that connection between their products and, say, deaths from heatwaves. “But now the science is at the point where we can make those connections clearly. That is a story the industry does not want told.” The Guardian approached Glencore, a partner in the HVO mine, for comment, but received no response.
